chapters.name: Pallet Town to Pewter
chapters.blurb: Pick a starter, deliver Oak's Parcel, get through Viridian Forest. Brock is badge one.

chapters.name: Mt. Moon to Cerulean
chapters.blurb: Mt. Moon, Nugget Bridge and Bill. Misty is badge two.

chapters.name: Vermilion and the S.S. Anne
chapters.blurb: Underground Path, Cut from the S.S. Anne, the Old Rod. Lt. Surge is badge three.

chapters.name: Rock Tunnel to Celadon
chapters.blurb: Rock Tunnel, Lavender, Celadon and the Rocket Hideout. Erika is badge four.

chapters.name: Pokémon Tower to Fuchsia
chapters.blurb: Silph Scope, Poké Flute, both Snorlax, the Safari Zone. Koga is badge five.

chapters.name: Saffron and Silph Co.
chapters.blurb: Clear Silph Co. Sabrina is badge six.

chapters.name: Seafoam and Cinnabar
chapters.blurb: Surf south past Seafoam to Cinnabar. Blaine is badge seven.

chapters.name: Sevii Islands 1 to 3, then loose ends
chapters.blurb: Bill takes you to One Island. Back in Kanto, Route 21 and the Power Plant before Giovanni.

chapters.name: Victory Road and the League
chapters.blurb: Route 23, Victory Road, the Elite Four.

chapters.name: Postgame
chapters.blurb: National Dex, Sevii Islands 4 to 7, Cerulean Cave, the legendaries.

tips.63: Teleports away on turn one. Throw a ball immediately (catch rate 200) on Route 24/25, or skip the hassle and buy one at the Game Corner for 120 coins.
tips.113: Safari Zone only: 1% in Center, 4% in North (Area 2). Throw one Bait first, since it raises Chansey's catch odds and cuts its 45% flee chance.
tips.128: Safari Zone only, 4% in West (Area 3) and 1% in North (Area 2). Throw Bait: at catch rate 45 it doesn't lower your odds, and it cuts the 45% per-turn flee chance to 10%.
tips.115: Safari Zone only, 4% in East (Area 1) and 1% in West (Area 3). Same bait-first approach as Tauros.
tips.127: LeafGreen exclusive. Safari Zone Center 4% or East 1%, or buy it at the Game Corner for 2500 coins (Lv18) to avoid the Safari gamble.
tips.123: Not obtainable in LeafGreen at all. Trade from FireRed.
tips.147: Super Rod in any Safari Zone water (15%, Dragonair 1%), each catch spending Safari steps and balls. The Game Corner sells one for 4600 coins (Lv24) if you would rather grind coins.
tips.132: Pokémon Mansion B1F (10%), Routes 13 to 15, or Cerulean Cave. It turns into a copy of your lead Pokémon, so lead with something that won't hurt your own team; catch rate 35.
tips.137: No wild encounter in either version. Game Corner only, 6500 coins (Lv18) in LeafGreen.
tips.143: Two chances (Routes 12 and 16), Lv30, catch rate 25. Save first; running or knocking it out removes it permanently. Sleep it and chip it down, and watch for Rest.
tips.101: The two fake-item Electrode in the Power Plant (Lv34) know Self-Destruct, and blowing itself up counts as a defeat, which removes it for good. Put it to sleep or paralyze it before it can move.
tips.92: Pokémon Tower ghosts can't be caught until you have the Silph Scope. Gastly is the common Tower encounter; Haunter appears higher up.
tips.144: Lv50, catch rate 3. Save first. Running makes them respawn when you re-enter, but knocking one out loses it, so chip with weak hits and use sleep or paralysis.
tips.145: Lv50, catch rate 3. Save first. Running makes them respawn when you re-enter, but knocking one out loses it, so chip with weak hits and use sleep or paralysis.
tips.146: Lv50, catch rate 3. Save first. Running makes them respawn when you re-enter, but knocking one out loses it, so chip with weak hits and use sleep or paralysis.
tips.150: Lv70, catch rate 3, knows Recover. Bring a sleep or paralysis user and lots of Ultra Balls (or the Master Ball). Running lets it respawn; fainting it does not.
tips.243: Only one per save and it flees every turn, so Mean Look or Block it, or use the Master Ball. On GBA, never let Entei or Raikou use Roar: if it escapes that way it is gone forever.
tips.244: Only one per save and it flees every turn, so Mean Look or Block it, or use the Master Ball. On GBA, never let Entei or Raikou use Roar: if it escapes that way it is gone forever.
tips.245: Only one per save and it flees every turn, so Mean Look or Block it, or use the Master Ball. On GBA, never let Entei or Raikou use Roar: if it escapes that way it is gone forever.
tips.201: Tanoby Chambers (Seven Island) after solving the Sevault Canyon Tanoby Key. Each chamber holds different letters, so you have to visit all seven for every form.
tips.131: The Silph Co. gift is the easy one. Wild Lapras surf in Icefall Cave's back cave at only 1%; FRLG has no clock, so there is no Friday rule.
tips.133: One gift only. FRLG has no day/night clock, so Espeon and Umbreon cannot be evolved here; trade to Ruby/Sapphire/Emerald for those.
tips.106: Choose one at the Dojo; the other needs a trade.
tips.107: Choose one at the Dojo; the other needs a trade.

tips.140: Mutually exclusive fossil choice at Mt. Moon. Trade for the other.
tips.108: Trade only in LeafGreen, and the Route 18 trader wants a Slowbro (Golduck in FireRed).
tips.151: Event only; not needed for the Kanto diploma.

oak.how: Talk to him in his lab, or use PROF. OAK's PC on any Pokémon Center PC.

say: You've barely started! Pokémon live in every patch of tall grass. Go and look!
Come back when your Pokédex has a little more in it.
Good, you're on the right track.
One of my aides on Route 2 has HM05 Flash waiting for you. Go see him!
Hmm, still a bit thin.
Try catching kinds you haven't met yet, not more of the same. My aide in the Route 10 Pokémon Center has an Everstone for you.
I can tell you're working hard at this.
My aide in the Route 11 gate has an Itemfinder for you. Very handy for hidden items!

tiers.short: Amulet Coin from the Route 16 aide
say: It's really coming along now!
Visit my aide in the Route 16 gate. He's holding an Amulet Coin for you.

tiers.short: Exp. Share from the Route 15 aide
say: Over fifty kinds! Splendid!
My aide in the Route 15 gate has an Exp. Share with your name on it.
Now this is starting to look like a proper Pokédex.
Keep it up!
Very good indeed!
Have you tried fishing? Plenty of Pokémon hide under the water.
Wonderful! You must really love collecting.
Don't forget to evolve what you've caught. Each new form counts!
Ninety-odd kinds! That can't have been easy.
I'm honestly impressed.
A hundred! I can hardly believe it!
You're in rare company now.
Marvellous. And you've raised plenty of evolved forms too.
That's the sign of a real trainer.
Excellent work!
For the ones you can't find here, trade with a friend. Some only live in FireRed.
Outstanding! You've become a true expert.
Only a handful left now.
There's nothing left for me to teach you.
At this point, you're the professor!
You did it! The Kanto Pokédex is complete!
Thank you. You've made an old man's dream come true. Go see the game designer in Celadon Mansion for your diploma!

extra: National Dex: enter the Hall of Fame with at least 60 Kanto Pokémon caught and having visited One Island, then talk to Oak in his lab.
Kanto diploma: catch all 150 (Mew doesn't count), then talk to the game designer on the top floor of Celadon Mansion.
Missing from LeafGreen entirely, trade from FireRed: Ekans, Arbok, Oddish, Gloom, Vileplume, Psyduck, Golduck, Growlithe, Arcanine, Shellder, Cloyster, Scyther, Electabuzz.

plan.title: Mt. Moon to Misty
team: Ivysaur. Razor Leaf at Lv 22 is your Misty plan.
Use the Moon Stone now, before Lv 22, so Nidoking learns Thrash at 22 (and Megahorn at 43).
Pikachu's Thundershock is a backup for Starmie.

prep.t: Route 3: beat the trainers along the way for EXP (Bug Catchers, Youngsters, Lasses).
Buy the Magikarp in the Route 4 Pokémon Center for ₽500. It's your Water stand-in until Robin joins.
Route 4 tutors outside Mt. Moon: Mega Punch (one-time) for Usopp. Mega Kick is the riskier option.
Mt. Moon 1F: TM09 Bullet Seed in an item ball. Luffy can use it.
Pick up both Moon Stones (1F item ball, B2F hidden) and use one on Usopp right away. Nidoking learns Thrash at Lv 22 only if he's already evolved.
Take the Helix Fossil at the end of Mt. Moon B2F.
Cerulean: heal up, then go north toward Nugget Bridge.
Your rival leads into a Charmander. Fire beats Luffy, so send Usopp or Pikachu.
Beat Misty: Cascade Badge (lets you use Cut) and TM03 Water Pulse.

plan.title: Vermilion and Lt. Surge
team: Ivysaur resists Electric. Teach him Cut.
Nidoking. Immune to Electric, so he's your Lt. Surge answer. Give him Dig.
Butterfree. Sleep Powder at Lv 15 for catching; Confusion meanwhile.
Pidgeotto (Pidgey, Lv 18). Optional; Flying helps vs Erika.
Pikachu. Optional; useful vs the rival's Pidgeotto, useless vs Surge.

prep.t: Nugget Bridge (Route 24): beat all five trainers, then the Team Rocket grunt for a Nugget. Sell it for ₽5,000.
Routes 24 and 25: catch Abra (throw a ball on turn one) and Bellsprout. Beat the Route 25 hikers and campers.
Bill's Sea Cottage at the end of Route 25: help Bill, get the S.S. Ticket.
Bill's PC: after getting the ticket, leave the house and come back in, then check the PC. Open Eevee, Flareon, Jolteon and Vaporeon; each counts as seen.
Cerulean: the burgled house is now open. Beat the Rocket grunt behind it for TM28 Dig. Teach it to Usopp.
Route 5: the Day Care is here if you want to park a Pokémon.
Route 6 to Vermilion: beat the trainers on the way.
Vermilion Pokémon Fan Club: listen to the chairman for the Bike Voucher.
Vermilion house: the Fishing Guru gives the Old Rod.
Vermilion house: trade a Spearow for Farfetch'd.
S.S. Anne 2F, first cabin: talk to the gentleman. He shows you Snorlax, which counts as seen.
S.S. Anne: beat your rival, then see the captain for HM01 Cut. The ship leaves after you get off.
Teach Cut to Luffy.
Back in Cerulean: trade the Bike Voucher at the Bike Shop for the Bicycle.
Cut the tree blocking Vermilion Gym. Beat Lt. Surge: Thunder Badge (lets you use Fly) and TM34 Shock Wave.
Diglett's Cave (east end of Route 11): catch Diglett, come out on Route 2.
Route 2 east (Cut): Oak's aide gives HM05 Flash at 10 caught. Trade an Abra for Mr. Mime in the house.
Pewter Museum back door (Cut): the scientist gives you the Old Amber.
Evolve Caterpie into Butterfree and Pidgey into Pidgeotto as you go.

plan.title: Rock Tunnel to Erika
team: Vulpix + Fire Stone. Burns Erika's whole team.
Doduo on Route 16. Press B to stop it evolving at Lv 31 until it learns Drill Peck at Lv 37 (Dodrio waits until 47).
Pidgeotto. Flying beats Erika's grass types until Sanji's ready.

prep.t: Route 9 (Cut the tree east of Cerulean): beat the trainers.
Route 10 Pokémon Center: Oak's aide gives an Everstone at 20 caught.
Rock Tunnel: dark without Flash, but walkable. On B1F a tutor teaches Rock Slide (one-time).
Lavender Town: heal. The Pokémon Tower needs the Silph Scope, so come back later.
Route 8, then the Underground Path to Route 7: catch Vulpix on Routes 7 or 8. It becomes Sanji.
Celadon Dept. Store 4F: buy a Fire Stone (Sanji) and a Thunder Stone (Nami).
Celadon Dept. Store 3F: a tutor teaches Counter (one-time).
Celadon Mansion: back entrance, roof room, take the Eevee. It becomes Nami.
Celadon Mansion 1F: the old lady gives you Tea. You need it to get into Saffron later.
Celadon restaurant: a man gives you the Coin Case.
Route 16 (Cut the tree west of Celadon): catch Doduo, the future Zoro. The house there gives HM02 Fly.
Route 16 gate 2F: Oak's aide gives the Amulet Coin at 40 caught.
Beat Erika: Rainbow Badge (lets you use Strength) and TM19 Giga Drain for Luffy.
Game Corner: the poster hides the switch to the Rocket Hideout. Get the Lift Key on B4F, beat Giovanni, take the Silph Scope.
Game Corner prizes (coins): TM24 Thunderbolt, TM35 Flamethrower, TM13 Ice Beam, plus Abra 120, Clefairy 750, Pinsir 2,500, Dratini 4,600, Porygon 6,500.

plan.title: Pokémon Tower to Koga
team: Drill Peck at Lv 37 if you held off evolving.
Butterfree. Psybeam at Lv 34 is super effective on Koga's Poison types. Out once Robin joins.

prep.t: Pokémon Tower (Silph Scope): beat your rival on 2F, calm the Marowak ghost, rescue Mr. Fuji at the top.
Lavender: Mr. Fuji gives you the Poké Flute.
Route 12: wake Snorlax with the Poké Flute. Save first; it's a one-time Lv 30 catch.
Route 12 gate 2F: a girl gives TM27 Return.
Route 12 fishing house (south of Snorlax): the younger Fishing Guru gives the Super Rod.
Routes 13 and 14: grass behind Cut trees has Ditto. Beat the trainers.
Route 15 gate 2F: Oak's aide gives the Exp. Share at 50 caught.
Route 15 gate 2F: look through the left binoculars. Articuno counts as seen.
Fuchsia: the Fishing Guru's brother gives the Good Rod. The Substitute tutor is in town too.
Fuchsia zoo: read every enclosure sign. Chansey, Voltorb, Kangaskhan, Slowpoke, Lapras and Kabuto (the fossil you didn't take) all count as seen.
Safari Zone: find the Secret House (HM03 Surf) and the Gold Teeth. Chansey, Kangaskhan, Tauros, Pinsir and Dratini live here.
Fuchsia Warden's house: give him the Gold Teeth for HM04 Strength.
Route 16 Snorlax: your second chance. Then Route 17 Cycling Road (Bicycle) and Route 18.
Route 18 gate 2F: trade a Slowbro for Lickitung.
Pokémon Tower 5F: a hidden Big Mushroom that's always there, for Luffy's Sleep Powder later.
Beat Koga: Soul Badge (lets you Surf) and TM06 Toxic.

plan.title: Silph Co. and Sabrina
team: Bench for Sabrina: Psychic hits Poison hard.

prep.t: Give the Tea to a Saffron gate guard to get in.
Fighting Dojo: beat everyone, then take Hitmonlee or Hitmonchan.
Mr. Psychic's house: TM29 Psychic for Robin.
Silph Co.: find the Card Key on 5F to open the locked doors. A tutor on 2F teaches Thunder Wave.
Silph Co. 7F: beat your rival. A worker gives you Lapras, the future Nico Robin.
Silph Co. 11F: beat Giovanni. The president gives you the Master Ball. Save it for Mewtwo or the roaming beast.
Copycat's house: the Mimic tutor (bring her a Poké Doll from the Dept. Store).
Beat Sabrina: Marsh Badge (lets you use Rock Smash) and TM04 Calm Mind.
Surf south from Fuchsia down Routes 19 and 20.
Seafoam Islands: push the Strength boulders to slow the currents. Articuno (Lv 50) is on B4F. Save first.
Cinnabar: Pokémon Mansion. Find the Secret Key on B1F; it opens Blaine's gym.
Cinnabar Lab: revive the Helix Fossil (Omanyte) and the Old Amber (Aerodactyl).
Cinnabar Lab trades: Ponyta for Seel, Venonat for Tangela, Raichu for Electrode.
Cinnabar Lab research room: the Metronome tutor.
Beat Blaine: Volcano Badge (lets you use Waterfall later) and TM38 Fire Blast.
Talk to Bill on Cinnabar; he takes you to One Island. Celio gives you the Tri-Pass.
Kindle Road, Ember Spa: the old man gives HM06 Rock Smash.
Mt. Ember: beat the Team Rocket grunts at the entrance. The Explosion tutor is outside.
Mt. Ember summit: Moltres (Lv 50). Save first.
Two Island Move Reminder: one Big Mushroom or two Tiny Mushrooms gets Luffy's Sleep Powder back.
Cape Brink house (Two Island): with Venusaur in the lead at max friendship, Luffy learns Frenzy Plant.
Three Island: Bond Bridge, then Berry Forest to rescue Lostelle (Hypno battle).
Back to One Island and Celio, then Bill takes you home to Kanto.
Route 21 (Surf from Pallet or Cinnabar): Tangela in the grass.
Power Plant (Surf from Route 10): Zapdos (Lv 50). The two 'item balls' are Electrode. Save first.

plan.title: Giovanni and Route 22
team: Surf and Ice Beam (Lapras learns it at Lv 31).
Bench vs Giovanni: Ground hits her hard.

prep.t: Viridian Gym is open now. Beat Giovanni: Earth Badge and TM26 Earthquake for Usopp.
Route 22: beat your rival. His Charizard is Lv 53.
Route 23: show your badges at each gate.

plan.title: Victory Road and the Elite Four

prep.t: Victory Road: Strength boulders onto the switches. A tutor on 2F teaches Double-Edge.
Indigo Plateau mart: stock Full Restores, Revives and Hyper Potions. Save before the Elite Four.
Lorelei (Ice): Nami's Thunderbolt and Sanji's fire.
Bruno (Fighting): Zoro's Drill Peck; Robin's Surf for his Onix.
Agatha (Ghost): her Gengar float (Levitate), so skip Earthquake. Robin's Psychic, Nami for Golbat.
Lance (Dragon): Robin's Ice Beam does 4x to Dragonite.
Champion: Charizard Lv 63 goes to Robin; Nami takes Gyarados; Sanji or Zoro take Exeggutor.

crew: Sleep Powder, Razor Leaf, Giga Drain (TM19 from Erika), Cut
Drill Peck, Tri Attack, Agility, Fly
Thunderbolt (TM24), Double Kick, Pin Missile, Flash
Flamethrower (TM35), Confuse Ray, Quick Attack, Fire Spin
Surf, Ice Beam, Psychic (TM29), Body Slam

crewLines.where: Eevee, Celadon Mansion roof room + Thunder Stone
Nidoran♂, Route 3 or the Route 5 trade
